newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU agrees "spy in sky" fish satellite system.
newsitem.headline: EU agrees "spy in sky" fish satellite system.

text.p: European Union fisheries ministers struck a political agreement on Thursday to set up a satellite system for monitoring fishing vessels, EU officials said.
"Agreement was achieved quickly after Italy lifted its objections," an EU official said, adding that a legal text would be agreed early in 1997.
Italy's change of mind meant that opposition from Denmark, Spain, the Netherlands and Sweden could be overridden under the EU's weighted voting system.
Italy came on board after receiving a pledge of EU aid from July 1997 for Italian driftnet fishermen hunting swordfish in the Mediterranean to retire or switch to other activities, officials said.

Satellites will start to track fishing vessels in certain areas from June 30, 1998 and the system will become fully operational from January 1, 2000, when all vessels over a total length of 24 metres, fishing more than 12 miles offshore and for longer than 24 hours will be tracked.
Satellites will transmit information back to the home countries which will then pass it on to the country in whose waters the boats were fishing.
Capital investment costs will be covered from a 205-million- Ecu ($254 million), five-year EU fisheries control fund.
Spain, which has the biggest fishing fleet, will be the most affected with 1,000 large, distant-water vessels subject to satellite controls, or 25 percent of the total.
Italy would have 800 vessels tracked and the Netherlands 350.
Pilot projects carried out between July 1994 and December 1995 showed that satellites considerably strengthened fishing controls, the Commission said.
